findings.current_text: Rendered inside the sentence ui.library.preview.unsupported ONLY via the generic fallback; see manifest.
findings.problem: ENGLISH METADATA, not the translation. The note says this label is rendered inside the unsupported sentence via the generic fallback, but the generic sentence has no kind slot, so the label is never interpolated there at all: src/renderer/src/features/library/components/library-viewers.tsx:107-111 branches on asset.kind === 'other' to t('ui.library.preview.unsupported_generic') with no parameters. A translator reading 'rendered inside the sentence ... via the generic fallback' can reasonably infer that the word will sit in a grammar slot and pick a form to fit (here 'دیگر' would have produced 'دیگر فائل کا پیش منظر…', 'another file's preview'), which is the wrong inference. UnUR-damaged only because the translator chose rightly; the note is still misleading. 'see manifest' is also a dangling reference for a translator - the keys20 manifest lives in an audit worktree, not the repo.
findings.recommendation: Rewrite to: "Never interpolated into ui.library.preview.unsupported: kind `other` takes the slot-free generic sentence ui.library.preview.unsupported_generic, so this label appears as a badge only." and drop 'see manifest' or name the file.
evidence: src/renderer/src/features/library/components/library-viewers.tsx:105-106 comment: "`other` is the catch-all: 'A Other file' is ungrammatical in English and worse in translation, so it gets its own sentence with no kind slot."
src/i18n/catalogues/en/ui.library.context.json: ui.library.preview.unsupported_generic note = "Shown when the file kind is the catch-all `other`; no placeholders."

findings.problem: قسم is also this namespace's rendering of the sort option 'Kind' (ui.library.sort.kind = قسم), so the English distinction the sidecar asks for ('Keep it distinct from the sort option Kind') is collapsed. But this is the corpus's own settled practice, not a divergence introduced here: both 'Type' and 'Kind' already render قسم in separate surfaces. نوعیت would be the distinct Urdu word and appears nowhere in the catalogue today, so the change is free if the team wants the distinction; nothing forces it. Recorded so the decision is visible rather than accidental - does not gate.
findings.recommendation: No change required. If the distinction is wanted, use نوعیت for the tag heading and record the call in the ur guide; otherwise leave قسم and record that Kind/Type share one Urdu word.
evidence: grep for نوعیت across src/i18n/catalogues/ur/: no matches

findings.problem: The Tags section now shows the heading ماخذ a few rows below the filter section mاخذ (ui.library.filter.source) whose rows are origin groups - two identical headings in the same rail with different contents. This mirrors the English exactly ('Source' for both), and ماخذ is this catalogue's settled word for source, so the translation is correct; the ambiguity is the English information architecture's, which the sidecar itself flags. Recorded for the manager; no translation change recommended (disambiguating here would break the one-term-one-decision rule in the opposite direction).
findings.recommendation: No change. If the rail is ever reworked, disambiguate in English first (for example 'Tag source'), then translate.
evidence: src/renderer/src/features/library/components/library-filter-rail.tsx:302-307: the tag heading renders inside <Section label={t("ui.library.filter.tags")}> as a text-meta text-ink-dim span above that group's rows
